variants.headline: Looking back: party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The leader of {party}, {leader}, had blundered in an election debate.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. An error in a debate and a result at an election are distinct events. The report should not imply a measured change in support or attribute a particular response to the public without an adequate basis.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We defend {target} against an exaggerated verdict. A debate mistake does not erase the merits of a political position, and fairness requires more than turning an awkward moment into a complete judgment.

variants.headline: Looking back: a debate brings a leader's misstep
variants.sub: The party leader {leader}, of {party}, has made a debate misstep.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: An election debate had included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. An error in a debate and a result at an election are distinct events. The report should not imply a measured change in support or attribute a particular response to the public without an adequate basis.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We defend {target} against an exaggerated verdict. A debate mistake does not erase the merits of a political position, and fairness requires more than turning an awkward moment into a complete judgment.

variants.headline: Looking back: election argument meets an awkward moment
variants.sub: The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate.
